# IEC 60812 — Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA and FMECA)

_Demo sample data — not for clinical use._

**Standard**: IEC 60812:2018 (3rd edition, published 2018-08)
**Category**: Risk analysis methodology (reliability engineering)
**Recognized by FDA**: Yes — Recognition Number 5-120, Complete standard, STG General I (QS/RM), Recognition List 051 (entry 2019-01-14)
**Registry distillation (L1a)**: [`.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60812.md`](../../../.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60812.md) — what the standard says; this file covers what the PP3500 program has decided about it.

## Overview

IEC 60812:2018 defines how FMEA and its criticality variant FMECA are planned, performed, documented, and maintained — for hardware, software, processes (including human action), and their interfaces. It is a generic reliability-methodology standard, not a medical-device standard: in this program it supplies the FMEA **method**, while risk acceptability and the overall risk process remain governed by ISO 14971:2019 (see [`iso-14971.md`](./iso-14971.md)). See the L1a registry distillation for the method elements, the 2018 edition's treatment of RPN alternatives and criticality matrices, and public-source citations.

## PP3500 Applicability

IEC 60812:2018 is the **methodology anchor** for the program's bottom-up failure analysis:

| Artifact | Role | Anchor |
|----------|------|--------|
| [`GL-WI-RM-002`](../../internal/source-md/risk-management/fmea-wi.md) — FMEA Work Instruction | Defines the step-by-step dFMEA/pFMEA method (parent SOP GL-SOP-RM-001) | §1: "Methodology anchored in IEC 60812:2018" |
| [`GL-TMP-RM-004-design-fmea.md`](../../project/dhfs/pca-device/risk-management/GL-TMP-RM-004-design-fmea.md) — PP3500 dFMEA | Bottom-up design failure analysis; links upward into hazard analysis (GL-TMP-RM-003) | Standards Anchor: ISO 14971 §5; IEC 60812 |
| [`GL-TMP-RM-004-process-fmea.md`](../../project/dhfs/pca-device/risk-management/GL-TMP-RM-004-process-fmea.md) — PP3500 pFMEA | Bottom-up manufacturing/production failure analysis ahead of pre-Transfer review | Standards Anchor: IEC 60812; 21 CFR 820.75 |

FMEA is used here as a **tool inside** the ISO 14971 process — complementing the top-down hazard analysis (GL-WI-RM-001 / GL-TMP-RM-003), never substituting for it. Every FMEA failure mode with patient-harm potential links to a hazard analysis row via the `Linked Hazard ID` column.

## Local Adaptation — Scoring and RPN Policy (GL-STD-RM-001 §9)

The QMS adapts the IEC 60812 method with an explicit boundary on how prioritization measures may be used:

- **Scales**: Severity (S) per the GL-STD-RM-001 §3 five-level clinical-outcome scale; Occurrence (O) 1–5 using the §4 probability anchors as a proxy; Detectability (D) 1–5 per §9 (D=1 detected before harm → D=5 undetectable until harm occurs).
- **RPN is prioritization-only**: per [`GL-STD-RM-001`](../../internal/source-md/risk-management/risk-assessment-criteria.md) §9, the composite RPN (S × P × D) is used for *prioritization within an FMEA only* — final residual-risk acceptability is judged against the §5 risk-acceptance matrix (S × P), never against an RPN threshold. GL-WI-RM-002 §4 restates this: S and O drive acceptability; D prioritizes mitigation effort and cannot discount an unacceptable risk. This is consistent with ISO 14971 §5.5's definition of risk as severity × probability of harm, and with the 2018 edition's own documented caution around arithmetic RPN products (see L1a).
